_label: Evidence archive: public postings of Metaconceptual Art (2011-2012)

identified_by.content: Evidence archive: public postings of Metaconceptual Art (2011-2012)

content: Two public postings on the text-hosting service Pastebin, made under the account LIVINGART8 and still publicly readable, carry Metaconceptual Art before 2013. The earlier, titled 'The Art World is Flat', was posted on 2011-11-28 at 07:51:51 CDT. It presents a poem which its author introduces as a metaconceptual Art poem written some years earlier and published free to the world that day in honour of Cyber Monday 2011, and it links to a Sun & Rain Works page on Facebook. The later, titled 'MetaConceptual Art', was posted on 2012-11-22 at 23:19:57 CDT. Headed '#WTF is MetaConceptual Art ?!' and carrying the same Facebook link, it sets out 'The 8 Defining characteristics of Metaconceptual Art' as a numbered list of eight sentences. Those eight sentences are the work catalogued in this collection as Eight Sentences On Metaconceptual Art, and they agree with the published text word for word, differing only in a comma, a space, and the spelling of 'Transcendance', later normalised to 'Transcendence'. These postings establish that the term, the eight-part definition, and the studio's attachment of both to Sun & Rain Works were public and fixed in a third party's records on 2012-11-22, and that the term was already in use as a settled description on 2011-11-28.

referred_to_by.content: Evidence status: publicly verifiable on a third-party platform, and the earliest such evidence in this collection. The postings are readable by anyone at https://pastebin.com/AmQ3P87v and https://pastebin.com/18ndp2CF ; both are set never to expire. Their dates are assigned by the platform at the moment of posting and are carried in the page markup as 'Thursday 22nd of November 2012 11:19:57 PM CDT' and 'Monday 28th of November 2011 07:51:51 AM CDT'. Unlike a profile biography, the body of a paste is fixed once posted. The platform also records public circulation: 950 views for the 2012 posting and 433 for the 2011 one at the time of compilation. Nothing here is studio-held, so verification requires no access to the private archive.

Relation to the published Eight Sentences. The 2012 posting is the earliest located instance of the sentence sequence and predates its publication on this site by fourteen years. That there were eight characteristics is attested twenty-three days earlier, in a private Facebook message of 2012-10-30 which refers to them without listing them, set out in the record of the 2012-2013 Facebook and USA Projects evidence. Its wording is the wording published here, allowing for three trivial variances: 'commodification of Art, and its relationship' has since lost its comma, 'the Art World , and Art History' has lost a space, and 'Transcendance' has been corrected to 'Transcendence'. The persistence of a misspelling across the interval, and its later silent normalisation, are recorded because they are the sort of detail by which a text's descent is traced. The sequence's stated debt to Sol LeWitt's 'Sentences on Conceptual Art' is not present in the 2012 posting and appears to be a later framing.

A second, independent timestamp for the 2011 posting. The studio's Facebook account data, compiled by Facebook on request on 2026-09-24, records that at 2011-11-28 15:44:21 UTC the account 'liked' a link titled 'The Art World is Flat - Pastebin.com', pointing to http://pastebin.com/18ndp2CF, the posting described above. That is within three hours of the posting time Pastebin displays, 07:51:51 AM on the same day. The like is Facebook's record, made on its own servers, so the posting's date no longer rests on Pastebin's alone, and it shows the posting being marked from the studio's own account on the day it was made. The entry is in the export's reactions file, 4,891,632 bytes, SHA-256 b4199322474511c9db9892c812ff17ec641702b8aee7826e6944bdbf15c57924, within the archive facebook-joechirum-2026-09-24-TZ87gGfq.zip, SHA-256 c978c3bd338a6a9a934d3aa05a81d2c298c49200bf7e4edc98b8329c02103097.

Limits. Both postings are the artist's own; the platform dates when he said something publicly, not whether what he said was true. They therefore evidence the public existence of the term and its definition at those dates, and nothing about the 2009 auction, which neither posting mentions. The 2011 posting describes its poem as written 'a few years ago', which would place composition somewhere in the late 2000s; that is the artist's own statement, made in 2011 rather than in retrospect from the present, and it narrows but does not close the gap to the asserted 2007 origin. The origin date itself remains unevidenced. Both postings link to a Sun & Rain Works page on Facebook. That page has since been deleted by the studio, and the Internet Archive holds no capture of it, so it cannot be examined and any earlier material it carried is lost. Its former existence is not in doubt: the 2012 posting cites its address and presents the eight characteristics as the page's content, which places the definition on that page on or before 2012-11-22. The postings recorded here are consequently the surviving witness to a source that no longer exists, and they are load-bearing for that reason.

Preservation note. Of the sources that once carried this material, several no longer exist: the Facebook page has been deleted, the YouTube videos cited in the 2013 correspondence are gone, and the mailbox from which that correspondence was sent has been closed. What survives does so on a third-party platform the studio does not control, in two postings set never to expire. Their continued availability is not guaranteed by anyone. The studio has therefore taken a local copy of both postings - the paste bodies and the rendered pages, the latter retained because they carry the platform's own timestamp string that the raw endpoint omits - published alongside this record with checksums at data/evidence/pastebin-2011-2012/. Those files are a preservation copy and not the dated source: a local file proves what was retrieved and when it was retrieved, and nothing more. The dating rests on Pastebin's records, which assign a posting timestamp the poster cannot alter, and should be verified against the live URLs for as long as they resolve.

Context for November 2011, independently dated. The studio states that in the autumn of 2011 it set up and ran two wiki sites for the Occupy movement, at wikioccupy.org and wikioccupy.com. Part of that is verifiable without reference to the studio: the Internet Archive first reached wikioccupy.org on 2011-10-24, captured pages of the running wiki on 2011-10-25, and captured its main page, 'Wiki Occupy Home', on 2011-10-31, which gives as its contact an address at the site's own domain under the name 'Art'. No capture of wikioccupy.com exists, and both domains have since lapsed and are now unregistered. An earlier version of this record gave a capture of 2011-12-03 as the earliest and read it as the live site; that capture returns only the hosting provider's default page, and the earlier captures were found when every address under the domain was searched. The site and the chat logs of November 2011 in which the studio principal described it as art are set out in the record of www.wikioccupy.org.

What that context does and does not do. It does not evidence Metaconceptual Art. Running a wiki for a protest movement is not making art, and nothing on the archived site has been shown to concern the studio's work. Its relevance is to reading, not to dating: the posting of 'The Art World is Flat' on 2011-11-28 was made in the same weeks that its author was, on independent evidence, operating web infrastructure for a movement whose subject was finance and inequality. A poem about the flatness of the art world, published in honour of Cyber Monday by someone then running an Occupy wiki, is more legible for knowing that. Two smaller points also follow. The studio's account of the wiki is a claim it did not control the checking of, and it checks out, which is a modest reason to take its other accounts of that period seriously. And a person who registered and ran domains for projects in 2011 is the kind of person who might have done so for www.wtfisart.com in 2009, which makes that claim more plausible in kind without dating it by a single day.

An outstanding lead, recorded so it is not lost. The studio holds three chat logs downloaded from meetings of that period, sent to a correspondent on 2012-11-12 as attachments named for their dates: two of 2011-11-10 and 2011-11-19, and a third of 2011-11-19. Those dates fall eighteen and nine days before the posting of 2011-11-28, which is the earliest located public use of the term; an earlier, private use, of 2009-12-19, is set out in the record of the 2009 Facebook evidence. The logs have not been examined. If the term, the eight characteristics, or the concept in recognisable form appears in them, the earliest evidence in this collection moves earlier, and it moves into a different and better kind of source: conversation with other people, rather than the studio's own solo posting. If it does not appear, that is a negative worth recording with the same care.
